comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Hypothesis-driven pass 1 (worktree deer-flake, git 2.55 local; CI failure was git 2.54/ubuntu, pytest 9.1.1 + xdist 3.8.0).

MECHANISM FINGERPRINT (proven by direct injection): building the exact fixture history and unlinking .git/objects/66/842fd0... between the 1005 commit and the merge reproduces the CI signature EXACTLY — rc 128, 'error: invalid object 100644 66842fd0... for aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd/1005-cccc2222-COMMENT.json' printed TWICE, 'fatal: git write-tree failed to write a tree'. Also verified: json.dumps of the fixture's 1005 payload hashes to 66842fd0... — git add hashed the CORRECT bytes; the object then went missing.

Discriminators proven:
- A zero-length/corrupt loose object does NOT reproduce it: merge exits 0 (the write-tree check is stat-only). The CI failure therefore requires ENOENT — the loose file (or its fanout dir) was ABSENT at merge, milliseconds after 'git commit' of the same blob succeeded (commit's own write_index_as_tree verifies the blob too, so it was present at commit time).
- gc --auto / gc / prune / repack -adq run between commit and merge do NOT reproduce it: the blob is reachable (packed, still findable), merge succeeds. gc cannot prune a fresh reachable object; auto-gc threshold (~6700 loose) is unreachable in a ~30-object repo. Hypothesis (b) as *normal, completed* maintenance: KILLED. A background maintenance process remains conceivable only as a crashed/interrupted repack, but nothing in this repo triggers maintenance at all pre-merge.

(a) GIT_* env leakage: KILLED. grep of the whole suite + src: no os.environ direct assignment of GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY/GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES/GIT_COMMON_DIR anywhere; all GIT_* settings are monkeypatch.setenv (function-scoped, main-thread reverted) of harmless keys (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM, GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH, GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES). Also logically inconsistent: a leaked object-dir during add+commit of 1005 would strand the COMMIT+TREE objects in the alternate store too, and the merge would then fail resolving HEAD, not at write-tree with only the blob missing.
(c) global git config: KILLED. CI writes only identity + init.defaultBranch (all workflows grepped); nothing destructive; no test writes --global (the two --global reads are env-isolated).
(d) tmp_path 30-char truncation collision: KILLED. Suite-wide scan of all test defs truncated to 30 chars: neither test_a_git_failure_falls_back_ nor test_ledger_attribution_is_unc has a duplicate; failing dirs were _0 (first use). Workers own disjoint popen-gwN basetemps; both CI steps use distinct basetemps and run sequentially.

Selection-bias note: this fixture's merge (trivial in-index merge -> write-tree) is one of the only operations in the 13k-test suite that VERIFIES loose-object presence for a whole directory, so ANY rare loose-object disappearance anywhere in the suite would preferentially surface at exactly this line — consistent with two hits in this module (both ubuntu, both popen-gw1) and nowhere else.

Next: bounded stress reproduction attempt, then (per plan) the instrumentation path if the deleter stays unidentified.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Hypothesis pass 2 + resolution (instrumentation path).

STRESS: 30 further iterations of the module under -n 4 --dist worksteal (210 fixture instantiations) on macOS/git 2.55 — all green. Combined with oropendola's ~29,400 executions, no organic reproduction exists.

xdist worker-restart angle (evaluated, dead end): a crashed worker's basetemp rmtree could in principle race a sibling — but restarts require --max-worker-restart (not set; default = no restart), the failing run shows no worker crash, and each worker owns a disjoint popen-gwN basetemp. Also, the failing tmp dir (_0, first use) is created milliseconds before use with a unique name no other process learns, so cross-test targeted deletion is impossible; the deleter must be in-process, a git child, or ambient — all instrumentable.

MECHANISM (proven by injection, deleter unidentified): unlinking the loose object between commit and merge reproduces the CI signature byte-for-byte (doubled 'invalid object' + 'fatal: git write-tree failed to write a tree', rc 128). Corrupt-but-present object => merge rc 0 (presence check is stat-only). hash-object confirms git add hashed correct bytes. So: ENOENT on a fresh loose object, cause unknown.

LANDED (Gerrit change 1769): the ticket's instrumentation path. _GitFailed now carries an object-store forensics snapshot captured at failure time — git fsck --full, git count-objects -v, recursive .git/objects listing with sizes+mtimes, GIT_* environment — rendered in the exception, best-effort (capture failure never masks the original error), type stays CalledProcessError. Withheld-oracle TDD: regression test reproduces the proven mechanism (delete loose object -> merge) and went RED on each forensic section before the implementation; 4 manual mutants (no attach, no render, no fsck, no listing) all killed. make lint + make typecheck green. Next CI occurrence will name the missing objects, show what survived with mtimes, and rule env redirection in or out — pinning the deleter instead of restarting the hunt.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Phase 1 RCA for the third organic recurrence — confirmed test-harness defect.

The new signature is not the prior missing-loose-blob class. In a real fixture repo, deleting the exact 1005 loose blob (66842fd006b2fdc95ff55a33a263f1cb216bc7d6) left BOTH the directory-wide git log and the immediate per-event git log healthy: broad rc=0/stdout=804 bytes; narrow rc=0/one SHA. Therefore the earlier ENOENT mechanism cannot produce this batched-empty/narrow-success recurrence.

The changeable defect is the equivalence test at tests/unit/test_authorship_batched_ticket_map_7084.py:184 treating one raw call to build_ticket_position_commit_map as guaranteed non-empty even though the function contract at src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:294-378 explicitly returns {} on any Git/process/empty-output failure and production callers fall back per event. The repository already records that Git reads can transiently return rc!=0 or empty stdout under CI load and require bounded recovery (tests/_git_counts.py:1-55). The CI observation is exactly one empty batched result followed immediately by a successful per-event read in the same repo.

Discriminating runtime injection reproduced the complete observed sequence for every single-attempt transient boundary: first rc=128/empty stderr payload, rc=0 with empty stdout, and BlockingIOError(EAGAIN) each made the raw batched helper return {}; an immediate replay of identical argv against unchanged state returned all 8 positions (rc=0, 804-byte stdout). Three other CI lanes and the local fixture use the same deterministic topology successfully, ruling out a stable parser/topology defect. The lower-level transient class is intentionally fail-closed and may be rc, empty output, or process-spawn pressure; the test bug is requiring that optimization-only call to succeed on its first environmental attempt instead of using bounded recovery while retaining a loud persistent-failure diagnostic.

Defect legitimacy: defect in the test harness, not production authorship behavior. The production contract preserves attribution via per-event fallback; the test should isolate the equivalence property from a documented transient Git-read boundary. Phase 2 will be test-only: add bounded exact-call recovery for fixture-backed batched-map assertions, inject the first-attempt transient as the RED oracle, preserve persistent-failure diagnostics, and leave src/rebar unchanged.

comments.body:
Phase 2 RED oracle and contract card. authoritative_contract: raw batched resolver may fail closed to {} (src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:294-378), while fixture equivalence must remain deterministic across documented transient Git reads (tests/_git_counts.py:1-55). trigger_preconditions: the first real broad git-log boundary returns rc128/empty, rc0/empty, or raises EAGAIN; the identical second attempt runs normally against the unchanged real fixture repo. production_path: test-local fixture resolver -> real build_ticket_position_commit_map -> real temp Git history. tier: real temporary repository with fault injection only at the subprocess return boundary; a pure mock would not prove the real parser/topology succeeds on replay. observable_postcondition: all 8 exact position->SHA pairs equal the per-event resolver, with exactly two broad attempts. negative_control: a persistent empty result stops after exactly five attempts and raises diagnostics containing fsck and count-objects output. collateral_invariants: production authorship source and fallback semantics remain unchanged. gate: make test.

Final oracle was observed legitimately RED before the fix: rc128, empty-success, and EAGAIN cases each failed because broad_calls was 1 rather than 2; the persistent case failed because no AssertionError was raised. pytest collected and executed all four cases (4 failed, 8 deselected in 1.96s). The behavioral failures are the missing bounded recovery/diagnostic behavior, not import or fixture errors.

Final repair report.

Problem: Gerrit 1827 failed because the raw fixture-level batched map was {}, although an immediately following per-event read succeeded in the same repository.

Proven root cause: tests/unit/test_authorship_batched_ticket_map_7084.py required a one-shot optimization helper to return a complete map even though src/rebar/attest/authorship.py explicitly fails closed to {} on any Git/process/empty-output transient and production callers fall back per event. The deterministic test harness lacked the bounded Git-read recovery already established by tests/_git_counts.py.

Proof: deleting the previously implicated 1005 loose blob left both broad and narrow history walks healthy (broad rc=0, 804-byte stdout; narrow rc=0, exact SHA), refuting the prior ENOENT class. Runtime injections of rc128/empty, rc0/empty, and BlockingIOError(EAGAIN) each reproduced the organic sequence: first batched {}, immediate identical replay returns all 8 entries. The same deterministic topology was green in the other CI lanes, ruling out a stable parser/topology defect.

Test: the held-out real-temporary-repository oracle covered all three transient classes plus persistent bounded failure. It was RED first (four failures for missing second attempt/diagnostic), GREEN after the fixer, and returned to four RED failures under the exact omitted-recovery mutation before being restored. ## Context / Scope Correction
This ticket originally tracked a loose-object ENOENT/write-tree failure. When Gerrit 1827 later failed with a batched-empty / narrow-success signature, the ticket was reopened under the assumption that it was the same failure class. Investigation refuted that assumption: deleting the previously implicated loose blob left both broad and narrow history walks healthy. The unresolved ENOENT symptom is preserved separately in previous-quelled-nutria, linked discovered_from this ticket and blocked on recurrence evidence. Historical comments below remain the audit trail; the current scope is only the distinct Gerrit 1827 recurrence.

## Problem
In Gerrit 1827 run 31961655783, tests/unit/test_authorship_batched_ticket_map_7084.py called build_ticket_position_commit_map once and required a complete map. That optimization helper explicitly fails closed to an empty map on any Git nonzero result, empty output, or process exception; production callers then preserve attribution with per-event fallback. The fixture equivalence assertion incorrectly treated the optimization boundary as guaranteed to succeed on its first environmental attempt. The observed sequence was an empty batched result followed immediately by a successful narrow read in the unchanged repository.

## Approach
- Prove the recurrence boundary with the real temporary Git topology and first-attempt injections for rc 128 with empty output, rc 0 with empty output, and BlockingIOError(EAGAIN).
- Add fixture-only bounded recovery that repeats the exact batched resolver call, returns only a complete map, and stops after five attempts with existing object-store diagnostics.
- Route both direct equivalence assertions and the optimization-count assertion through the same fixture helper.
- Keep src/rebar fail-closed and per-event fallback behavior unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] The prior loose-object ENOENT class is refuted for this recurrence: deleting the implicated blob leaves both broad and narrow history reads successful; the residual ENOENT work is tracked in previous-quelled-nutria.
- [x] First-attempt rc 128/empty, rc 0/empty, and BlockingIOError(EAGAIN) injections each reproduce the observed empty-batched then successful-identical-replay sequence against the real fixture repository.
- [x] Fixture-only recovery makes at most five exact batched attempts, returns on the first complete map, and raises persistent diagnostics containing fsck and count-objects evidence; no src/rebar behavior changes.
- [x] Both fixture equivalence assertions and the optimization-count assertion use the recovery seam without weakening exact position-to-commit expectations.
- [x] Held-out TDD evidence is recorded: four behavioral cases were RED before the repair, GREEN afterward, and returned to RED under the exact omitted-recovery mutation; the in-file optimization sibling was independently RED then GREEN.
- [x] [operator-attested] Focused tests (12 passed), adjacent suites (27 passed), lint, typecheck, and the full local suite (13,522 passed, 60 skipped, 289 deselected) are green; Gerrit 1828 earned LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 with zero unresolved comments, merged as commit 29448f61c095c4f63afb9291ae156a4e0163d843, and CI run 31967631562 completed with 17 green jobs including Ubuntu/Python 3.11.
